tasks.name: Erdos minimum overlap
tasks.description: Choose equal-width step heights h on [0,2], bounded between 0 and 1 with integral 1, to minimize the maximum overlap of h with shifted 1-h.
tasks.contract: construct() -> sequence of step heights in [0, 1] whose sum is exactly len/2; score is the upper bound on C5

tasks.name: Lennard-Jones cluster global minimum, 38 atoms
tasks.description: Place 38 atoms interacting through the Lennard-Jones potential (reduced units) to minimise the total energy. LJ38 is the classic hard case of cluster optimisation: the global minimum is a face-centred-cubic truncated octahedron (energy -173.928427, Cambridge Cluster Database) while the icosahedral funnel traps local searches. The evaluator computes the energy exactly; the seed is a cubic lattice fragment.
tasks.contract: construct() -> array of shape (N, 3): Cartesian coordinates of N atoms in reduced Lennard-Jones units (sigma = 1). Atoms must be at least 0.5 apart. Score: total Lennard-Jones energy 4*sum(r^-12 - r^-6) over all pairs, minimized. science_chemistry.relax(positions) (L-BFGS local relaxation) is available to candidates.

sources.locator: Wales and Doye 1997, Global optimization by basin-hopping and the lowest energy structures of Lennard-Jones clusters containing up to 110 atoms.
Cambridge Cluster Database (LJ global minima table, doye.chem.ox.ac.uk/jon/structures/LJ/tables.150.html): N=38, point group Oh, energy -173.928427; inspected 2026-09-20.

limitations: The database values are putative global minima found by extensive searches, not proven optima; the reference is reproduced in tests by constructing the fcc truncated octahedron and relaxing it.
Reaching -173.928427 reproduces a known structure; a lower energy would be a new putative minimum and must be verified independently.

tasks.name: Climate dynamics: partial-observation Lorenz-96 assimilation
tasks.description: Design an ensemble analysis update that reconstructs an evolving twenty-variable chaotic state from noisy observations of half its coordinates. The evaluator propagates the ensemble and compares each updated ensemble mean with independent high-accuracy reference trajectories.
tasks.contract: analyze(ensemble, observations, observed_indices, observation_variance) -> updated ensemble with the same (16,20) shape. Lorenz-96 dx_i/dt=(x_(i+1)-x_(i-2))*x_(i-1)-x_i+F with periodic indices, nondimensional units. Evaluator propagates each member by RK4 at dt=0.01 for five steps between updates, then observes even-indexed states with independent N(0,0.49) noise. Three runs F=6,8,10, seeds=181,283,389; 40 updates each. Score is pooled analysis-mean RMSE against independent DOP853 truth over all states and cycles. Output must be finite and within [-100,100]. Use assimilation_case with seeds=41,53,67 for development; no truth or future observations are provided to analyze.

sources.locator: Tomizawa and Sawada (2021), Combining ensemble Kalman filter and reservoir computing to predict spatiotemporal chaotic systems; Section 2.1 Eq. (1) Lorenz-96 dynamics and Section 2.2 ensemble data assimilation.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic twin experiments, not weather observations or the paper's reservoir-computing results.
Local reduced dimensions, seeds, observation noise, spin-up, perfect-model forcing and short duration are documented in the contract. Longer-horizon stability and forecast skill are not established.
All evaluation seeds are public. Use fresh seeds and forcing regimes after freezing the candidate for a generalization claim.

tasks.name: Climate dynamics: unresolved-tendency closure
tasks.description: Fit a shared degree-five polynomial approximation to the unresolved fast-scale forcing of a two-scale Lorenz-96 model. Train on supplied slow-state/tendency pairs and minimize normalized error on independent validation trajectories, including an unseen forcing regime.
tasks.contract: construct(training_x, training_subgrid_tendency) -> 6 finite real polynomial coefficients in ASCENDING powers of local slow state x, approximating the unresolved tendency as sum(c_i*x**i). Inputs are flattened paired samples from two independent spun-up trajectories at F=6,8. Reference uses Rasp (2020) two-scale Lorenz-96 with K=8,J=4,h=1,c=10,b=10: dX=advection-X+F-h*c*mean(Y); dY=c*(-b*Y_(j+1)*(Y_(j+2)-Y_(j-1))-Y+h*X/J). Fast indices form one periodic K*J ring, crossing slow-cell boundaries. Score is mean validation MSE/variance(true tendency) over three independent trajectories at F=6,8,10. Units nondimensional. Coefficients must be a single shared polynomial for every cell and forcing.

sources.locator: Rasp (2020), Section 4.1 Eqs. (2)-(3), slow/fast model and closure target; Section 2 discusses offline versus online evaluation.

limitations: Local polynomial/offline adaptation with reduced K=8,J=4; not the paper's neural-network coupled-training protocol or a score reproduction.
Training and validation trajectories use distinct initial seeds; F=10 is absent from training, but all generators are public.

A deterministic local polynomial cannot recover every fast-scale tendency from the slow scalar alone. Lower offline error does not establish stable coupled forecasts or resolve cloud-feedback uncertainty.

tasks.name: Cosmology: compact dark-energy growth approximation
tasks.description: Improve a six-coefficient growth-index formula for the linear growth rate and normalized growth factor in smooth CPL dark-energy cosmologies. A tightly integrated general-relativistic second-order ODE provides an independent numerical reference. The score is the worst relative error across both observables on disjoint public validation cosmologies, extending the constant-gamma seed within a fixed compact ansatz.
tasks.contract: construct() -> real vector of six finite coefficients in [-10,10]. At scale factor a, q=1-Om(a), u=1+w0+wa*(1-a), gamma=c0+c1*q+c2*q^2+c3*u+c4*wa*a+c5*u*q, and f=Om(a)^gamma. Gamma must lie in [0.1,1.2] at all checked locations. The evaluator computes D(a)/D(1)=exp(-integral_ln(a)^0 f(exp(x)) dx). Minimize 100 times the maximum relative error of both f and normalized D over validation models and a values.

sources.locator: Linder and Cahn, Parameterized Beyond-Einstein Growth; equations 1-3 and 8: growth-index ansatz and GR growth equation; equations 14-15: constant growth-index approximation.
Linder, Exploring the Expansion History of the Universe; equations 6 and 7 and following density evolution define the CPL background.

limitations: Local synthetic approximation task, not an observational discovery or reproduction of a paper's fitted coefficients.
Uses general relativity, flat space and smooth dark energy; excludes nonlinear structure, modified gravity, radiation and neutrino effects.
The numerical reference uses the explicitly specified finite matter-era boundary D(ai)=D_x(ai)=ai at ai=0.001; it is not a full Boltzmann cosmology solver.
Calibration and validation models are disjoint but public. Better scores establish accuracy only on this finite model set and do not resolve the dark-energy problem.

tasks.name: Cosmology: universal luminosity-distance quadrature
tasks.description: Discover an eight-node positive quadrature rule for dimensionless luminosity distance in spatially flat, time-varying dark-energy models. The same nodes and weights must work across all models. Minimize the worst relative error against independent adaptive integration on disjoint public validation cosmologies. This is a locally designed synthetic numerical-method task reconstructed from published distance and CPL equations.
tasks.contract: construct() -> {'nodes': length-8 real vector, 'weights': length-8 real vector}. Nodes must be strictly increasing in [0,1], weights positive and sum to 1 within 1e-12. One universal rule is used for every cosmology: dL/(c/H0) = (1+z)*z*sum_i weights[i]/E(a_i), where a_i=1/(1+z*nodes[i]) and E(a)=H(a)/H0. The evaluator computes integrands itself. Minimize worst relative validation error in percent; exactly eight integrand samples per distance.

sources.locator: Hogg, Distance measures in cosmology, v4; sections 4, 5 and 7, equations 15, 16 and 21: comoving and luminosity distance.
Linder, Exploring the Expansion History of the Universe; section B, equations 6 and 7 and following density evolution: w(a)=w0+wa(1-a).

Develops and compares Romberg and Gaussian quadrature for luminosity distance in CPL dark-energy models. The fixed universal eight-node rule and public cosmology split are local restrictions on that same numerical-method problem.

limitations: Local reduced benchmark, not original paper code, measurements, or a reproduction of a published benchmark score.
Assumes a flat matter plus smooth CPL dark-energy background; omits radiation, spatial curvature and neutrino effects.
The calibration and validation cosmologies are disjoint but public; repeated optimization against validation can overfit this finite suite.
The metric tests numerical accuracy at fixed eight-sample inference cost, not measured speed or a resolution of the dark-energy problem.

tasks.name: Expansion-history models fitted to the Pantheon+ supernova Hubble diagram
tasks.description: Propose a parametric expansion history E(z) = H(z)/H0 with at most six parameters and fit it to the 1,580 Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova light curves with zHD > 0.01 (the 1,590-object cosmology sample minus the ten Cepheid-host calibrators) (corrected apparent magnitudes and the full statistical plus systematic covariance). The absolute magnitude is profiled analytically; the score is the minimum chi-squared, lower is better. Flat LambdaCDM with a fitted matter density is reported for comparison.
tasks.contract: expansion(z, theta) -> array E(z) = H(z)/H0 for an array of redshifts z >= 0 (positive, finite; E(0) should be 1); initial_theta() -> initial parameter vector (1 to 6 values); bounds() -> list of (low, high) per parameter. The evaluator fits theta to the Pantheon+ Hubble diagram (zHD > 0.01 and no Cepheid calibrators: 1,580 light curves, STAT+SYS covariance) with the absolute magnitude profiled analytically and H0 = 70 fixed for the distance scale; score is the minimum chi-squared (lower is better). Flat LambdaCDM (fitted Omega_m) chi-squared is reported for comparison.

sources.locator: Brout et al. 2022, The Pantheon+ Analysis: Cosmological Constraints; Section 2 (data), Section 3 (likelihood with the STAT+SYS covariance, zHD > 0.01 cut).
Pantheon+SH0ES.dat and Pantheon+SH0ES_STAT+SYS.cov, fetched by scripts/prepare_science_data.py and pinned by SHA-256.

limitations: Real measurements: the data are the public Pantheon+ release, fetched at prepare time (network), not redistributed.
The likelihood profiles the absolute magnitude and fixes H0 = 70 for the distance scale, so only the shape of E(z) is constrained; the SH0ES Cepheid calibrators are excluded.

A lower chi-squared than LambdaCDM with more parameters is not by itself evidence for new physics; model comparison needs an information criterion or Bayesian evidence, which the evaluator reports the ingredients for (chi-squared and parameter count).

tasks.name: Quantum information: shallow-circuit Ising ground states
tasks.description: Optimize parameters of a fixed three-layer Ry/CZ circuit to approximate ground states of open transverse-field Ising chains. The evaluator builds each state itself and minimizes the mean energy gap per spin relative to an independent exact eigensolution.

limitations: The source paper derives upper bounds with semidefinite programming. This task recreates its finite code-construction question and objective, not its SDP algorithm or experiments.

The 512..673 interval is dated source context, not a claim of an optimum or a permanently current record. The evaluator assumes only the elementary Hamming bound, derived directly from disjoint Hamming balls.
Improving the 32-word seed or reaching 512 words does not settle the open extremal problem. Any proposed new record needs separate comparison with current constructions and upper bounds.

tasks.name: Ramsey graphs for R(5,5): large graphs with no K5 and no independent 5-set
tasks.description: Construct a graph on as many vertices as possible with no clique of size 5 and no independent set of size 5. Every such graph on n vertices proves R(5,5) > n. The best known construction is Exoo's 42-vertex graph (R(5,5) >= 43) and Angeltveit and McKay proved R(5,5) <= 46, so the exact value is open. The seed is the Paley graph on 37 vertices, verified (5,5)-free by the evaluator.
tasks.contract: construct() -> (n, edges): the number of vertices and a list of (i, j) pairs with 0 <= i < j < n. The graph must contain no clique of size CLIQUE and no independent set of size INDEPENDENT; n must be at most MAX_VERTICES. Score: n, maximized (each valid graph proves R(CLIQUE, INDEPENDENT) > n).

tasks.name: Snake-in-the-box in the 9-dimensional hypercube
tasks.description: Construct the longest induced path (snake) in the hypercube Q_9: a sequence of distinct 9-bit vertices in which consecutive vertices differ in one bit and non-consecutive vertices differ in at least two bits. The exact maximum is known only up to dimension 8 (98 in Q_8); in dimension 9 the best known snakes had length 190 before 2026 and were improved in arXiv:2607.15270, so the problem is open. The seed is a greedy snake of length 104.
tasks.contract: construct() -> list of distinct integers in [0, 2**N): the vertices of an induced path in the hypercube Q_N in order. Consecutive vertices differ in exactly one bit; non-consecutive vertices differ in at least two bits. Score: number of edges, maximized.

sources.locator: Allison and Paulusma, New bounds for the snake-in-the-box problem: definitions, exact values up to dimension 8 (a(8)=98) and lower bounds.

Summary of known snake and coil lengths by dimension, inspected 2026-09-20.

limitations: The evaluator checks the snake property exactly; it does not embed a record construction, so the reference label is none.

tasks.name: Size-efficient sorting networks on 16 wires
tasks.description: Construct a fixed compare-exchange network that sorts all 16-input sequences using as few comparators as possible. Correctness is certified by the zero-one principle over all 65,536 Boolean inputs. Parallel depth is reported separately. A verified 60-comparator construction is the reference; the initial odd-even transposition network uses 120 comparators.
tasks.contract: construct() -> ordered list of integer pairs (i, j), 0 <= i < j < N. Each compare-exchange writes min to wire i and max to j. The network must sort every input. Score: comparator count, minimized; parallel depth is reported separately. Maximum 4096 comparators.

sources.locator: Codish et al., Sorting Networks: to the End and Back Again (2015/2016): comparator-network definitions, zero-one verification, and the optimal size/depth construction problem.
Author-maintained sorting-network list, 16 inputs / 60 compare-exchanges / 10 layers; inspected 2026-09-20. Comparator topology is preserved as an independently verified test fixture.

limitations: This is an independently recreated construction benchmark, not a reproduction of the paper's SAT search, experimental budget, or optimality proof.
The size objective is identical to the finite sorting-network problem. Depth is diagnostic only, and the 4096-comparator cap is a generous benchmark resource limit.

The 60-comparator reference is a verified feasible upper bound. The inspected source lists size bounds 57..60; this package does not prove the minimum or promise that the online record will remain current.

Improving the 120-comparator seed or recovering a published network is not a new research result. A claimed record requires a separately reviewed construction and comparison against current literature.

tasks.name: Biology: Single-cell batch integration: public scIB adaptation
tasks.description: Integrate measured count matrices across experimental batches while preserving cell-type neighborhoods and rare populations under a declared transductive protocol.
tasks.contract: integrate(counts, batch_labels) -> finite cells x dimensions embedding, 1<=dimensions<=128. No cell-type labels supplied. Transductive evaluation. Local scIB-inspired score =0.6 cell-type-macro kNN purity +0.4 within-cell-type batch mixing. Rare-type purity diagnostic. This is an adapted public scIB protocol, not reproduction of Station private scores.

sources.locator: scIB Methods: joint evaluation of biological conservation and batch correction.
Official author implementation/data reference; evaluator and seed are independently written, not copied.
Original scIB pancreas h5ad; rawcounts and genuine technology/cell-type annotations. Pinned SHA256 in data/science/biology_expansion/sources.json.

limitations: Measured scIB human-pancreas study:1000 hash-selected cells and500variable genes from raw-count layer,9genuine technology batches. Transductive local metrics, no fullscIB/Station score reproduction or cross-study claim.
Canonical Station upgrade using an explicitly adapted public scIB-style60/40 score. Does not reproduce the private Station evaluator or complete scIB metric suite; no trajectory conservation claim.
Public source subsets are development-visible. Freeze candidates before evaluating on additional independently chosen studies/instances; trusted candidate execution is not a security sandbox.
Improving this benchmark is a scientific-method result; it does not alone establish a new biological discovery.
provenance.benchmark: Biology: Single-cell batch integration: public scIB adaptation
provenance.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes
